newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases amid low demand.

text.p: Weaker demand for kuna funds lowered the average Croatian money market rate ten basis point to 9.3 percent on Wednesday.
Total settlements reached 27.2 million kuna, leaving a surplus of 7.8 million kuna on the supply side.
Dealers said new borrowings were made at a rate of 8.0-9.5 percent for call money and 12 percent for term loans.
Insurers rolled over previous short-term loans at a steady 8.0 percent rate.
Tuesday overnight trade totalled a high 97.7 million kuna, of which three banks used 66 million kuna to maintain their mandatory reserves. Another bank borrowed money to square its position.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday slightly weaker at 5.4433 against the dollar and 3.5605 against the German mark. --Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
